rationale:
Evidence: all 60 development trials ended off_track with no completions. Progress was only 0.06 to 0.17, and max_error (0.061 to 0.067) reached or passed the 0.06 m off-track limit. Each run recorded 2 line-loss events, and steering_oscillation was about 0.16 to 0.18. The error is larger than the sensor geometry alone explains, which points to the controller overshooting and oscillating at speed.

Changes: (1) base_speed 1.8 to 1.4. Lower speed reduces lag, overshoot and the chance of leaving the tape on the sharpest bends. Finishing still needs about 1.5 m/s on average, so this trades some completion-time score for a higher chance of finishing at all. (2) kp 5.0 to 4.0. This softens the steering response that is likely overshooting the centre line. (3) kd 0.3 to 0.6. More derivative action should damp the jitter that drives steering_oscillation. (4) ki 0.05 to 0.02. Less integral action avoids windup on the bends. (5) sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016. Larger footprints give the outer sensors some tape coverage at the edge of the line, which should reduce the 2 line-loss events per run. Sensor positions, weights, wheel and body geometry, and line_loss 'last_direction' are kept, so the controller changes are easier to attribute.

Expected result: fewer off-track exits and fewer line-loss events, with rms_error and max_error dropping below the 0.06 m limit on the oval and s-bend. Completion may still be marginal because of the lower speed. If progress rises but the runs still stall or leave the track, the next step is to adjust speed and kd together.
